== Biography ==
'''Emma Glasgow''' was reportedly born about 1815 in South Carolina. Her exact birth date, later life and parentage have not been established by an inspected contemporary record.

== Research Notes ==
=== Parentage ===

Emma remains attached as an uncertain daughter of [[Glasgow-2769|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-658277|Nancy Unknown]] because no better placement has been identified. A female under 10 in Robert's 1820 Giles County household and a female aged 20–29 in his 1840 Lauderdale County household are both compatible with Emma's reported birth year.<ref name="Census1820">1820 United States census, Giles County, Tennessee, Robert Glasgow household; NARA microfilm publication M33, roll 124; [https://archive.org/details/populationsc18200124unit/page/n21/mode/1up original schedule, scan 21].</ref><ref name="Census1840">1840 United States census, Lauderdale County, Alabama, p. 48, Robert ''Glasgow'' household; NARA microfilm publication M704, roll 7; [https://archive.org/details/populationsc18400007unit/page/n245/mode/1up original schedule, scan 245].</ref> Neither census names the woman, so the two-household fit supports the chronology but does not prove that she was Emma or Robert and Nancy's daughter.

A current FamilySearch Family Tree profile preserves the same derivative placement, but it does not provide a contemporary record identifying Emma.<ref name="ProjectSource1">FamilySearch Family Tree, [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/KNQV-BPB Emma Glasgow, KNQV-BPB] (accessed 29 August 2026).</ref>

=== Emma Glasgow’s marriage at Belfast, 1875 ===

A notice reports that Emma, daughter of the late William Alexander Glasgow, married William, second son of Robert Treacy, on 4 September 1875 at St Thomas’s Church, Belfast, with Rev T. J. Welland officiating. Both spouses were of Parsonstown. The notice states neither Emma’s age nor her mother.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1265675182/ Belfast Evening Telegraph, 4 September 1875, p.2].</ref>

Identification with the woman reportedly born about 1815 in South Carolina remains weak. The attached Robert and Nancy parentage is an unproved reconstruction from unnamed census women, so it is not a documentary exclusion; a marriage at about 60 is also not ruled out by an age-free notice. The alternative father candidate [[Glasgow-1387|William Glasgow]], born about 1810, could not father this Emma on those dates. He would require a different, later-born bride: these are competing family hypotheses, not an asserted parent–child pair.
